evidence.text: The page describes 老’s oracle form as a bent, long-haired person holding a staff, with 人, 毛 and 丨 identified in that analysis; it says the staff appears in 匕-like form in bronze graphs and can be miswritten 止. Later upper-part variation is reported, with 由 possibly phonetic in one Spring and Autumn form. These are source interpretations, not proof that 由 formed the original graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The entry reports an oracle-bone place-name use, 合集22246; bronze examples for an elder, ‘be old’, senior ministers and 老 used for 考 ‘father’; and Warring States bamboo-text examples including 舜乃老. The entry does not establish a semantic chronology linking the place name, ‘old’ and ‘father’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 說文解字, 老部 (Wikisource transcription)
evidence.text: The received Shuowen text glosses 老 as 考, says a person aged seventy is called 老, and analyzes the graph as 从人、毛、匕, explaining it through whitening facial and head hair. This is a historical lexicographic account, not direct confirmation of the oracle graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字/08 — 維基文庫

evidence.source: ShuoWen.org, 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.field: 老 entry, explanation and Duan Yucai note
evidence.text: Duan Yucai discusses the traditional reciprocal glossing of 老 and 考, and suggests the seal form may derive from 毛匕, with 人 not a separate element. This later commentary differs in graphic analysis from reading the three Shuowen components literally; it does not establish the oracle graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「老」

gaps: The supplied exact 老 oracle image candidate returned 404 and was excluded; the Commons bronze direct image fetch returned a cache miss, so that file is not proposed as a direct image asset. The Academia Sinica Western Zhou bronze record is a usable specific candidate, but its image URL could not be extracted from the web tool’s rendered page; no image item is returned because the required direct image URL was not verifiable.
No glyph pixels were visually inspected. The cited form descriptions and source labels establish candidate identity and provenance, not visual confirmation.

The CUHK page reports an oracle place-name use but its relationship to the lexical sense ‘old’ is unresolved; it gives no absolute date for that particular occurrence. Bronze and Warring States uses are reported, but their original artifacts or text editions were not inspected separately.

The dossier’s proposed cane-component explanation is supported as a pictographic interpretation by CUHK; the Shuowen three-part analysis and Duan Yucai’s alternative seal-form analysis are later accounts. No phonetic component is established for the earliest graph, and the 由 phonetic suggestion applies only to a reported later variant.

No phonetic component is asserted, so no ancient component-to-host sound relationship is claimed. The local modern Mandarin row for 老 was not independently validated against official Unihan during this pass; the direct official page was inaccessible.

The semantic link between ‘old’ and 老 used for 考 ‘father’ is not established in the inspected sources. Shuowen’s reciprocal gloss and 轉注 tradition are historical analyses, not a demonstrated chronology.

No bulk source reuse is recommended. The Xiaoxuetang notice grants CC0 for query-interface glyph images and glyph attributes, but no small versioned extract was prepared; the exact selected image direct URL was unavailable.

limitations.text: No direct historical glyph image URL was verified as usable in this run. The supplied oracle image candidate is explicitly unavailable after HTTP 404; the alternate Commons bronze image’s direct fetch returned a cache miss, while the Academia Sinica page yielded a specific late Western Zhou record and CC0 rights notice but no extractable direct image URL. Accordingly no image is proposed.
